As for His saying ﴿restricted in the way of Allah﴾, there are three opinions concerning it:

[One of them]: Ibn 'Abbas said: it means that the enemy and poverty prevented them from the way of Allah and from jihad, so they became restricted from it.

﴿The ignorant man thinks them rich because of their modesty. You know them by their mark. They do not beg of people persistently.﴾

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: He meant by it that they went out to war, and wounds befell them, so they became restricted from jihad because of the wounds.

Qatadah said – and it is the best of the opinions: its meaning is that they restricted themselves to jihad in the way of Allah, and left going out for trade and livelihood, and devoted themselves to war.

This is related concerning the People of the Suffah, who were about four hundred men. They gathered in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they had no families to shelter with and no property, and the Prophet (ﷺ) used to send people to them with the surplus of their food. They had devoted themselves to jihad in the way of Allah, and they said: "No expedition goes out without us going out with it." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿restricted in the way of Allah﴾.

His saying: ﴿they are not able to go about in the land﴾ – according to the first two opinions, this refers to going about in the land for jihad.

According to the third opinion, it is going about in the land for livelihood and trade.

His saying: ﴿the ignorant man thinks them﴾ – Mujahid said: the ignorant here is not the opposite of the knowledgeable; rather it is the one who has no experience or knowledge of their condition.

His saying: ﴿rich because of their modesty﴾ means: because of the contentment they have; whoever does not know them thinks them rich.

His saying: ﴿You know them by their mark﴾ – it was said: by the humility that was in them.

Al-Dahhak said: by the paleness of their complexions.

Ibn Zayd said: by the shabbiness of their clothes.

It was also said: by the trace of hunger and hardship.

His saying: ﴿They do not beg of people persistently﴾ means: insistently.

It was said: its root is from ilhaf; so ilhaf is asking in a general manner, as if he asks everyone he meets.

There is another opinion in it: that He meant by it the complete abstention from asking; for when one asks, he has pressed (alhafa). That is, they do not ask at all.

The evidence for this is that He said: ﴿rich because of their modesty﴾, and when one asks he is not modest. It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever asks while he has an uqiyyah has pressed (alhafa)." That is, he has forty dirhams.

It has also been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "For one of you to take his rope and gather firewood on his back is better for him than to ask people, whether they give or refuse."

His saying: ﴿And whatever good you spend, indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾ – its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 274:

And the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: This was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib. He had four dirhams, and he gave one dirham in charity by night, one dirham by day, one dirham in secret, and one dirham openly; so the verse was revealed as approval of his act and praise of him.

It has also been said: By "expenditure" here is meant the expenditure on horses in the way of Allah, for they are fed from that expenditure by night and by day, secretly and openly. Expenditure on horses in the way of Allah is a great door of good. It has been related in a hadith: "He is rewarded for their dung and their urine."

And the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They shall have their reward with their Lord, and no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾. Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 275:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those who consume interest (al-riba)﴾ means: those who take it. He expressed "taking" by "consuming" because it is taken in order to be consumed.

And His saying: ﴿They will not stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch﴾.

Al-khabt (خبط) is striking without evenness. It is said: "So-and-so strikes khabt 'ashwa'," when he follows a path he is not guided along. From this is the saying of the poet:

(I saw death like a blind-camel's striking: whoever it reaches, it takes; whoever it misses, lives long and grows old.)

Its meaning: the one who consumes interest will be raised on the Day of Resurrection like the drunkard, who stands at times and falls at others.

It has also been said: it is from the stumbling (takhabbut) of Satan, which is that he enters a person and throws him down.

Al-mass (المس) is madness, and al-khabt is the beginning of madness. Its meaning: he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection like one afflicted with a fit, and that is the sign of those who consumed interest on the Day of Resurrection.

His saying: ﴿That is because they said: "Trade is only like interest."﴾ He meant by them the Thaqif tribe, for they said, "Trade is only like interest."

﴿But Allah has permitted trade and forbidden interest.﴾ This is their answer.

His saying: ﴿So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists⦆ means: from consuming interest.

﴿Then for him is what has passed﴾ i.e., he is forgiven for what passed of it, ﴿and his affair is up to Allah. But whoever returns﴾ to consuming interest ﴿those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 276:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah deprives usury of blessing﴾. That is: He takes away the blessing of wealth, for lawful wealth has blessing, and unlawful wealth has no blessing.

It was also said: its meaning is that He nullifies the charity given from usury, ﴿and multiplies charities﴾ and increases charities, ﴿and Allah does not love any ungrateful sinner﴾. So "kaffar" (one who greatly rejects blessings, i.e., ungrateful) is one of great ingratitude, and "athim" (sinful) is one who commits much sin.

The Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, and establish prayer, and give zakat, will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾. And its interpretation has already been given.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 278:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest (riba), if you are believers﴾. This was revealed concerning Thaqif and the Banu Makhzum. They brought their dispute to Attab ibn Asid, the judge of Makkah. Thaqif said: "We only embraced Islam on the condition that the interest owed to us be waived and the interest we are owed remain in force." Attab wrote about this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then the verse was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then sent the verse to Attab so that he could recite it to them.

As for His saying, ﴿if you are believers﴾, it means: giving up interest is among the conduct of the believers.

It has also been said that its meaning is: if you are (truly) believers.

The verse is concerned with the abolition of the interest of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance). That is because they used to lend people money on the condition that they would increase the debt at the time of repayment. A man would lend to another and set a term for him, then when the term came due he would say to him: "Increase the debt for me and I will increase the term for you." This was the interest of the Jahiliyyah, and it is forbidden.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 279:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So if you do not do it, then be informed of war from Allah and His Messenger.﴾ That is: then be certain of it.

It is also read with a long vowel: "fa-ādhinū bi-ḥarbin min Allāh" (fa-ādhinū, "so announce/be informed"), meaning: inform others that they must abandon usury (riba), for you are at war with Allah and His Messenger. So when you know this, you have known it.

﴿And if you repent﴾ — that is, if you abandon the permissibility of usury (istihlal al-riba) and turn back from it — ﴿then you shall have your capital, [the] principal of your wealth﴾ — the excess is cancelled, and the principal of the wealth is granted to them.

He said: ﴿And if you repent, then you shall have your capital﴾ because, as long as they held usury to be permissible, what they possessed was spoils (fay') that did not belong to them, neither its principal nor its increase.

﴿You shall not wrong [others] nor be wronged﴾ — that is: you shall not wrong by seeking an increase, and you shall not be wronged by a reduction in your right in the principal of the wealth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 280:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if the debtor is in hardship, then let there be respite until a time of ease﴾. Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited: "And if the one who owes the debt is in hardship" (wa-in kana man 'alayhi al-dayn dha 'usra). ʿAṭāʾ recited: "then a respite (fa-nāẓira) until a time of ease."

The well-known reading is ﴿And if there is one in hardship﴾, meaning: and if one in hardship occurs, or: and if one in hardship is a debtor of yours, then let there be respite until a time of ease, meaning: then grant him respite until ease (al-yasār).

Nafiʿ recited "ilā maysura" with a ḍamma on the sīn (maysurah), and it is the same as the first in meaning.

Abū al-Yusr narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: "Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, Allah will shade him in His shade on a Day when there is no shade but His shade."

Abū Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet that he said: "There was a man among those before you who used to lend money to people. He said to his servant: 'If you find one in hardship, overlook him, perhaps Allah will overlook us.' So he met Allah, and He overlooked him."

The report is in the Ṣaḥīḥ collections.

﴿And if you give charity﴾, meaning by remitting the principal of the money you gave as a loan. ﴿It is better for you, if you only knew﴾.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: This is the last verse to be revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Ibn Jurayj said: He (ﷺ) lived only seven nights after it, and in another narration, nine nights.

It is related that when Jibril (peace be upon him) brought down this verse, he said: "Place it at the two hundred and eightieth verse of Surat al-Baqarah. This verse is a record, which Allah has recorded upon all creation."

﴿Then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾. This is clear in its meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 282:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you contract a debt for a specified term⦆ Ibn ʿAbbas said: I bear witness that the salam (advance sale) with a deferred, specified term is in the Book of Allah; the longest verse was revealed concerning it, and he recited this verse.

His saying: ﴿contract a debt⦆ means: deal with one another in debt, as it is said: "I dayantuhu" (I dealt with him on credit) when you deal with him on credit.

If it is said: His saying ﴿you contract⦆ already expresses dealing in debt, so why did He say "contract a debt"? It is answered: because the Arabs say "tadayana" meaning "we exchanged and reciprocated," even if it is not in debt; so He said ﴿between you a scribe write it justly, and let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him; so let him write, and let the one who owes the debt dictate, and let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not diminish anything of it. But if the one who owes the debt is foolish, or weak, or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate justly⦆ "contract a debt" (so that the intended meaning of the word is known), and it is possible that He said it for emphasis. ﴿For a specified term⦆: al-ajal (the term) is a known period with a beginning and an end. This includes the term in salam (advance sale), the term in the price, and the term in a loan. Most scholars did not permit a term in a loan, but some permitted it.

﴿Then write it⦆: it was said that this is an obligation; this is the view of Mujahid.

Al-Shaʿbi said: writing is obligatory only when there is someone who can write. The more correct view is that it is recommended (mandub).

Abu Saʿid al-Khudri said: this command is abrogated by His saying: ﴿But if one of you entrusts another, let him who is entrusted fulfil his trust⦆.

His saying: ﴿And let a scribe write between you justly⦆. Writing justly means: writing without addition or reduction, and without advancing or delaying the term.

﴿And let no scribe refuse to write⦆: it was said that writing is obligatory upon scribes, on the apparent meaning of the verse; the more correct view is that it is recommended.

﴿As Allah has taught him, so let him write⦆: that is, as Allah has prescribed, so let him write.

﴿And let the one who owes the debt dictate⦆: al-imlal and al-imla' have one meaning.

Al-imlal is the dialect of Quraysh and Banu Asad, and al-imla' is the dialect of Qays and Tamim; both are mentioned in the Qur'an. So al-imlal here and al-imla' in His saying ﴿it is dictated to him morning and evening⦆.

﴿And let him fear Allah, his Lord⦆: meaning the one dictating. ﴿And not diminish anything of it⦆: and not reduce anything of the right.

His saying: ﴿But if the one who owes the debt is foolish or weak⦆. As for the foolish (safih): Mujahid said: it is the one who ﴿cannot dictate himself⦆ ... the ignorant one.

Al-Zajjaj said: he is one of weak intellect, and this includes the woman, the minor, and the like. From this is the poet's saying:

(They walk as spear-shafts sway, their tips swayed by the passing gusting winds.)

It was also said: the safih is the minor. The school of al-Shafiʿi holds that he is the squanderer who corrupts his wealth.

As for the weak (daʿif): he is one weak in intellect, from senility or madness.

﴿Or unable to dictate himself⦆: that is, unable to dictate due to muteness or blindness.

﴿Then let his guardian dictate justly⦆: meaning, the guardian of these.

As for those who did not permit placing the foolish under restraint, such as al-Nakhaʿi and Ibn Sirin and others, they said: by the guardian is meant the holder of the right; that is, if the one who owes the debt is unable to dictate, then let the one who holds the right dictate.

﴿And call upon two witnesses from among your men⦆: that is, and have them witness.

﴿But if they are not two men, then a man and two women⦆: meaning, if the two witnesses are not two men, then a man and two women.

﴿From among those you approve as witnesses⦆: they are people of merit and religion, as said by Ibn ʿAbbas. ﴿That if one of them errs⦆: that one of them forgets and is heedless, which is when her memory of the testimony lapses, or the testimony escapes her memory.

﴿Then one of them reminds the other⦆: this is by saying: "Were we not present at such and such a gathering? Did we not hear such and such?" ﴿The other; and let not the witnesses refuse when they are called, and do not be weary of writing it, whether small or large, along with its term. That is more just in the sight of Allah, more upright for testimony, and nearer to ensuring you do not doubt; except when it is a present trade⦆

Hamza recited: "in an tadilla fa-tudhakkira ihdahuma al-ukhra" (if one of them errs, then one reminds the other), as a conditional clause.

Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna said: "fa-tudhakkira ihdahuma al-ukhra" means: let one of them make the other a male, that is, they stand in the place of a man. The first view is more correct.

﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called⦆: it was said he meant: when they are called to bear witness; and he called them witnesses in the sense that they will be witnesses. It was also said: it is the calling to testimony.

﴿And do not be weary⦆: that is, do not become bored ﴿of writing it, whether small or large, along with its term⦆: meaning, whether the amount is little or much.

﴿That is more just in the sight of Allah⦆: more equitable in the sight of Allah ﴿and more upright for testimony⦆: because the writing reminds the witnesses.

﴿And nearer⦆: that is, that you do not doubt. ﴿Except when it is a present trade⦆: one reading has a dammah on the tā' as the subject of kāna (is), and another reads with a fatha on the tā', meaning: except when the trade is a present trade. A similar usage is the poet's saying:

(I ransom with my she-camel the sons of Dhuhl ibn Shaybān, when there is a day with bright, whitened stars.)

meaning: when the day is a day.

﴿That you conduct among yourselves⦆: meaning, when the trade is hand to hand.

﴿There is no blame upon you if you do not write it down; but call witnesses when you trade with one another⦆: this is a command of recommendation (istihbab).

﴿Let no scribe or witness be harmed⦆: ʿUmar recited "wa la yudarrar" and Ibn Masʿud recited "wa la yudarrar," while the well-known reading is "wa la yudar." This may be a prohibition to the scribe and the witness from causing harm, and it may be a prohibition to the one dictating and the one calling.

As for harming the witnesses and the scribe: it is that they refuse to write or to testify when called upon. As for harming the scribe and the witnesses: it is that they are called while busy, so that he is prevented from his work.

His saying: ﴿And if you do so, it is indeed a transgression in you⦆: that is, a disobedience on your part. (And fear Allah; Allah teaches you, and Allah is Knowing of all things.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 283:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe﴾. Ata' recited: "wa lam tajidu kitaban" (and you do not find writings), which is the plural of kātib (scribe), as one says qā'im (standing) and qiyam (standing ones), and nā'im (sleeping) and niyam (sleeping ones).

﴿then a pledge taken into possession﴾, and it is recited "fa-rihān" (pledges) maqbūḍah, and the meaning is one.

The ruling on pledging (rahn) is well known, and the mention of travel and the absence of a scribe is not a condition for the permissibility of pledging; rather, the statement came in terms of what is most general and most common (al-a'amm al-aghlab).

﴿And if one of you entrusts another, then let him who is entrusted discharge his trust﴾, meaning: if he entrusts him with a debt, then let him repay it on the basis of the trust.

﴿And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and do not conceal testimony﴾. He forbade the witnesses from concealing testimony, and it is forbidden.

﴿And whoever conceals it, indeed his heart is sinful﴾. It was said: Allah has not threatened anything with a threat like His threat concerning the concealment of testimony, for He said: ﴿indeed his heart is sinful﴾, and He intended by it the transformation of the heart, and we seek refuge in Allah. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 284:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, meaning, in ownership and dominion. ﴿And whether you reveal what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾. This is abrogated (mansukh), for it is related: When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, and they said: "Will Allah hold us to account for what we speak to ourselves?" They remained in that state for a full year. Then the words of Allah, may He be exalted were revealed: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ [2:286], and so this verse became abrogated by it.

This is the view of Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Mas'ud, and (Ibn 'Umar), and it is one of the two reports from Ibn 'Abbas.

The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not act upon it or speak it," meaning: speak it out.

The scholars of legal theory (ahl al-usul) said: this is not abrogated, because His saying ﴿Allah will call you to account for it﴾ is a report (khabar), and abrogation does not apply to reports; it applies only to commands and prohibitions.

Al-Walibi also related from Ibn 'Abbas, in the second report, that the meaning of His saying ﴿Allah will call you to account for it﴾ is: "He will make you know it," i.e., nothing of that is hidden from Him.

﴿So He forgives whom He wills﴾, meaning He forgives the believers, ﴿and punishes whom He wills﴾, meaning the disbelievers. ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers.﴾ This is because He mentioned the verses and the rulings, then said: The Messenger believes in all of that.

﴿Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. "We make no distinction between any of His messengers."﴾ Ya'qub (Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hadrami, one of the readers of the Qur'an) recited "lā yufarriqu" with the letter ya', meaning: the Messenger does not make a distinction between any of his messengers.

﴿And they say: "We hear and we obey."﴾ That is: we accepted. ﴿"Your forgiveness, our Lord."﴾ That is: forgive us, Your forgiveness; or: grant us Your forgiveness, our Lord. ﴿And to You is the final return.﴾ That is: the place of return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 286:

Allah's words: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, i.e., its ability (ṭāqa).

It has also been said: [it means] what is difficult (yashuqqu) for it. This is like a man's saying: "I cannot look at so-and-so," meaning: it is difficult for me to look at him. Likewise, mention of capacity (wus') here carries the meaning of ease, i.e., Allah does not burden a soul except with what is easy for it.

This verse is the one that abrogates (nāsikha) what we have explained.

﴿It shall have what it earned﴾, i.e., of good, ﴿and against it what it has earned﴾, i.e., of evil.

﴿Our Lord, do not call us to account if we forget﴾, i.e., neglect. It has also been said that it refers to literal forgetting.

﴿Or err﴾. Error (al-khaṭa') can mean deliberate intent, and it can mean literal error; one says akhṭa'a yukhṭi'u and khaṭi'a yakhṭa'u. What is meant here by "or err" is: that we intentionally do [wrong].

﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us﴾.

It has been said: it is the heavy covenant that was laid upon those before us.

It has also been said: do not lay upon us what is difficult for us.

It has also been said: the burden (iṣr) is a sin for which there is no repentance; i.e., protect us from a sin for which repentance is not accepted.

﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no capacity to bear﴾. In this there is evidence that Allah, exalted is He, may permissibly burden His servants with what they cannot bear; but He has only burdened the disbelievers with what they cannot bear, and has not burdened the believers. ﴿And pardon us﴾, i.e., wipe away from us; ﴿and forgive us﴾, i.e., cover [our sins] for us; ﴿and have mercy upon us﴾, i.e., show mercy to us.

﴿You are our Protector﴾: You are our helper and the one who manages our affairs. ﴿So give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾. Reports have been transmitted about the virtue of these two verses, among them what was narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever recites the last two verses of Surat al-Baqara in a night, they will suffice him."

It was also narrated that he (ﷺ) said: "They are two verses that were sent down from the treasure beneath the Throne."

And upon his family, all of them.
